# The Voice That Calls the Morning Star

## Scripture

"Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? ... while the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy?" — Job 38:4, 7 (NIV)

## Reflection

During these September nights, if you rise before dawn, look east. Venus often blazes there—the "morning star," bright enough to cast a faint shadow on moonless ground. It isn't truly a star, of course, but a planet reflecting the sun's light. Yet its brilliance has stirred poets and prophets for millennia.

In Job 38, God answers Job's anguish not with explanations but with questions—and one of them paints an astonishing picture: at creation, the morning stars *sang*. Before humanity existed, before Job's suffering, before our questions, the heavens were already worshiping. God's response to pain isn't always an answer; sometimes it's a reminder that the One who set the morning star in place is trustworthy even when we don't understand.

That is strangely comforting. Our seasons of confusion don't catch God off guard. The same voice that called Venus into its orbit, that steady point of light returning faithfully each dawn—that voice holds our lives too. The morning star doesn't struggle to shine; it simply reflects a greater light. So can we.

When answers don't come, worship can. Like those ancient stars, we can sing before we see the full sunrise.

## Prayer

Lord, when I cannot see Your purposes, help me remember that You laid the foundations of the earth—and You hold me still. Let my life reflect Your light faithfully, even in the waiting. Amen.
